What parts of our craft do we hold closest? Where do we want our skills and creativity to flex? Leaders in design, engineering, and product development sound off in [The Prompt](https://www.figma.com/blog/welcome-to-the-prompt/)

, a print and digital magazine by Figma’s Story Studio and Brand Studio—also available in the [Figma Store](https://store.figma.com/products/prompt-magazine). While you wait for your copy to arrive, dive into the stories below for a considered look at how AI might influence the way we build digital products.

## [What does good design mean now?](#what-does-good-design-mean-now)

With AI in the picture, it’s a more salient question than ever. Figma Vice President of Product Design, Noah Levin, and his team share their long-held craft principles and pragmatic approach to building with AI.

[![An abstract illustration of distorted trees raised on poles over a gradient background.](data:image/png;base64,)![An abstract illustration of distorted trees raised on poles over a gradient background.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/021d033930f0690ea051fe64e797b46078b965e7-696x914.png?w=528&h=693&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/what-is-good-design-in-the-age-of-ai/)

## [What can’t be commoditized?](#what-can-t-be-commoditized)

Being an engineer is about more than just outputting code, argues Figma Chief Technology Officer Kris Rasmussen: “It’s also about knowing which problems to solve and how to solve them.” His team reflects on how AI can foreground the art of the role.

[![An abstract illustration of colorful, tessellated bird shapes that grow more stretched as they rise.](data:image/png;base64,)![An abstract illustration of colorful, tessellated bird shapes that grow more stretched as they rise.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/63608707ff551b4fff5d127e220e783bfc80d3e1-1060x726.png?rect=1,0,1059,726&w=528&h=362&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/why-are-we-so-afraid-of-code-as-a-commodity/)

[**Read more**](https://www.figma.com/blog/why-are-we-so-afraid-of-code-as-a-commodity/)

## [What are you afraid to ask?](#what-are-you-afraid-to-ask)

Co-founder and CEO Aravind Srinivas calls his AI-powered search engine, Perplexity, a direct descendant of print encyclopedias and wikis—in other words, a source of judgment-free answers. In this interview, he describes how it works, what still needs improvement, and why human curiosity could use a copilot.

[![ Illustration of a conductor waving a baton at a robot playing the cello with a coastal landscape in the background.](data:image/png;base64,)![ Illustration of a conductor waving a baton at a robot playing the cello with a coastal landscape in the background.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/5494f02658beeafa4d026c1835929b3d9ff8ae48-1060x726.png?rect=1,0,1059,726&w=528&h=362&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/perplexity-ai-interview/)

## [Are we in the age of androids?](#are-we-in-the-age-of-androids)

From _Blade Runner_ to _Star Wars_, humanoid robots have long starred in the stories we tell about ourselves. Now, as androids step out of science fiction and into reality, we’re coming face to face with our fascination with AI. We sat down with builders of bots to learn what comes of embodied tech.

[![An illustration of a human form made up of pointillistic blue and purple dots.](data:image/png;base64,)![An illustration of a human form made up of pointillistic blue and purple dots.](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/a63734c092ef7b0e41726a417f06ed89711757c0-1060x726.png?rect=1,0,1059,726&w=528&h=362&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/are-we-finally-entering-the-age-of-androids/)

[**Read more**](https://www.figma.com/blog/are-we-finally-entering-the-age-of-androids/)

## [What is the power of print?](#what-is-the-power-of-print)

We aimed to find out with The Prompt, an 80-page magazine created in collaboration with Brand Studio and designer Chloe Scheffe. Printed on vellum, it interprets the issue’s themes through color, illustration, layout, and materiality. Limited-edition copies are available in the Figma Store.

## [Rabbit hole](#rabbit-hole)

[![A collage shows 1) a black and white illustration of a flower, 2) an illustration of two hands reaching for each other, one of which has six fingers, and 3) an pixelated illustration of a smiling robot](data:image/png;base64,)![A collage shows 1) a black and white illustration of a flower, 2) an illustration of two hands reaching for each other, one of which has six fingers, and 3) an pixelated illustration of a smiling robot](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/bf90c5e860155527eebb624114ddc361b4f89798-1300x730.png?rect=0,1,1300,729&w=804&h=451&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)](https://www.figma.com/blog/welcome-to-the-prompt/)

1\. Data points back to people. Director of User Experience Machine Learning at Google, Ovetta Sampson, double-clicks on [minimum viable data](https://www.figma.com/blog/what-is-minimum-viable-data/)

and the ethics of input.

2\. The creators of the Arc browser agree: Building anew means building for many—and that means opening up [the tech echo chamber](https://www.figma.com/blog/can-we-reach-beyond-the-echo-chamber/)

.

3\. How can AI reshape the physical realm? Icon co-founder and CEO Jason Ballard is starting with [3D-printed homes](https://www.figma.com/blog/should-robots-be-building-our-homes/)

.
